Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 29 of 2024

Applicant :- Sanjeev Singh
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief Secy. Home Deptt. Lko.

Counsel for Applicant :- Anil Kumar Yadav,Diwakar Singh Kaushik Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Aakash Prasad,Amitav Singh,Yash Joshi Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.
1.
Counter affidavit as well as supplementary counter affidavit/ short counter affidavit filed on behalf of the complainant are taken on record.
2. Under the orders of the Hon'ble Acting Chief Justice of date 11.1.2024 this case has been nominated to this Bench.

3. Learned AGA informs that he has procured complete instructions in the matter including upto date case diary and the charge sheet in this case so far as the applicant is concerned has already been submitted.

4. Heard Shri Anil Kumar Yadav, learned counsel for the accused/applicant, Shri Amitav Singh,
learned counsel for the complainant/ informant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

sentences.text:
This bail application has been moved by the accused/applicant- Sanjeev Singh for grant of bail, in Case Crime No. 0238/2023, under Sections 409, 411, 419 420, 468, 471, 504, 506 IPC & 65 Information Technology (Amendment) Act, 2008, Police Station Kurebhar, District Sultanpur,
during trial.
6. Learned counsel for the accused-applicant while pressing the bail application submits that it is a case of false implication.
The applicant has not committed any misappropriation of the money as shown in the FIR and in the statement of the prosecution witnesses.

7. Elaborating further, it is submitted that it appears that some misappropriation of money earmarked to be deposited in the A.T.Ms. have been misappropriated and in order to conceal the real culprit the soft targets have been alleged as accused persons including the applicant.

8. It is further submitted that except the presence of the applicant in various A.T.Ms. which have been found in the CCTV Footage there is no evidence with regard to the commission of the offence and the presence of the applicant in various ATMs is natural, so far as his duties are concerned.
9. It is also submitted that the recovery of of Rs. 1,00,000/- as shown on the pointing of the applicant may also not be believed in absence of independent public witnesses.
The said money was of the applicant and has been wrongly shown as the proceeds of the crime.

10. It is also submitted that identically placed co-accused persons, namely, Jaishankar Tiwari @
Samant Tiwari from whom Rs. 5,00,000/- are shown to have been recovered has been granted regular bail while Shri Ashish Pandey whose role is also identical to the instant applicant, has been granted anticipatory bail, by the Coordinate Benches of this Court, vide orders dated 20.12.2023 and 18.11.2023 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 14919 of 2023 and Criminal Misc.
Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.c. No. 2644 of 2023, respectively.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 14919 of 2023
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: 11. It is also submitted that another co-accused of the crime, namely, Rohit Singh has been granted anticipatory bail by this Court, vide order dated 8.1.2024 passed in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.c. No. 20 of 2024.

12. It is further submitted that criminal history of one case has been explained in paragraph 11 of the supplementary affidavit, however, the same is with regard to the personal dispute and is not connected with any misappropriated money or fraud etc.

13. It is further submitted that the applicant is in jail in this case since 17.9.2023 and there is no apprehension that the accused-applicant after release on bail, may flee from the process of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.
Charge sheet in this case has already been submitted.
14. Learned A.G.A. on the other hand submits that the applicant is accused of committing an heinous offence, therefore, he is not entitled to be released on bail.

Shri Amitav Singh, learned counsel for the complainant/ informant vehemently opposes the prayer of bail of the applicant on the ground that applicant was one of the main perpetrator of the crime and in total Rs. 1,36,76,500/- have been misappropriated by the applicant and another co-accused persons by hatching a conspiracy and thus having regard to the gravity of offences, the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail but he could not refute the submissions made on behalf of the applicant that identically place co-accused persons have been granted bail or anticipatory bail by the Coordinate Bench of this Court.

16. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it is reflected from the record that the applicant is stated to be an employee in the complainant's company and the job which was entrusted to the applicant and other co-accused persons named in the FIR was with regard to the custodian of the cash which was required to be deposited in various ATMs.
Allegations of misappropriation of money which was to be fed in the ATM has been alleged against the applicant.
Rs. 1,00,000/- is shown to have been recovered on the pointing out of the applicant from his house.
The said money has been claimed by the applicant as his own.
Identically placed co-accused person, namely,Jaishankar Tiwari @ Samant Tiwari and Ashish Pandey have been granted regular bail and anticipatory bail by the Coordinate Benches of this Court.

Rs. 5,00,000/-
were stated to have been recovered on the pointing of the co-accused Jaishankar Tiwari @ Samant Tiwari.
Another co-accused Rohit Singh has been granted anticipatory bail by this Court.

Nothing has been brought in the knowledge of this Court which may suggest that the orders of regular bail and anticipatory passed in favour of co-accused persons have been challenged at any higher forum or has been cancelled by the same Benches.
The applicant is in jail in this case since 17.09.2023 and criminal history of one case has been adequately explained.
Charge sheet in this case has already been submitted.
His presence may be secured before the trial court by placing adequate conditions.

17. Keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on the merits and demerits of the case, I am of the considered view that applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

18. Let the applicant- Sanjeev Singh involved in the aforesaid case be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(ii) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
19. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
